claims.text: High-entropy alloys treated at high pressure and high temperature will exhibit improved ductility relative to conventional alloys with similar compositions.
High-pressure high-temperature treatment induces a hierarchically patterned microstructure in high-entropy alloys.
A hierarchically patterned microstructure permits more efficient plastic deformation in high-entropy alloys.
A hierarchically patterned microstructure reduces the likelihood of crack propagation in high-entropy alloys.
More efficient plastic deformation and reduced crack propagation enhance the ductility of high-entropy alloys.
The strength-ductility trade-off remains a challenge for the proposed material and treatment.
The optimal high-pressure high-temperature treatment conditions have not yet been determined.
The relationship among treatment conditions, microstructure, and mechanical properties is not fully understood.
